title: A Phone Call from the Future Ended My 20-Year Marriage
author: Hibiscus City
synopsis:
Si Rong receives a mysterious call from the future, telling her that her husband of eighteen years has betrayed her. 

Si Rong refuses to believe it, but reality hits her hard. 

Not only is her husband, Shen Lan, having an affair, but even the adopted son and daughter she raised with such hardship are actually Shen Lan's children with another woman. 

What if she is forty? Si Rong decisively asks for a divorce.

Shen Lan does not believe that Si Rong, who loves him so deeply, would ask for a divorce. 

They have already lived half their lives together, and Si Rong is close to forty; what would she do without him? But Si Rong persists, and the two of them get their divorce certificate. 

On the first day, Shen Lan waits for Si Rong to regret it and come begging him to reconcile, after all, who would want a forty-year-old woman? 

One week after the divorce, Shen Lan panics. How could Si Rong...

chapters.title: Your Husband Has Betrayed You
chapters.content:
Si Rong half-reclined on a rattan chair to soak up the sun, taking occasional sips of rose tea, her apricot-shaped eyes narrowed in comfort.

Although she was approaching forty, many people who met Si Rong for the first time said she looked at most thirty.

All of this was due to the pampering of her husband, Shen Lan, whose provision made her life affluent and fulfilling, which was why she remained so youthful and vibrant.

Ring, ring, ring...

The sudden ringing of the telephone startled Si Rong. It was early 1996, and their household was among the first in Huaiyang County to have a telephone installed.

Yesterday, while playing with the phone, she had been regretting that her relatives and friends still didn't have phones in their homes, picking up the receiver and putting it right back down, not knowing who to call.

Now that the phone was ringing, who could it be?

Si Rong answered the phone, and a very familiar voice came from the other end, "Si Rong, I am you from twenty years in the future. Right now we only have a minute of talk time, and I will only say three things. First, divorce Shen Lan as soon as possible; he has betrayed you. Second, the two children you raised are ungrateful wretches; look out for yourself early on. Third, buy real estate, as much as you can."

Every single sentence here was explosive to Si Rong.

He has betrayed you!!!

Shen Lan?

No! She would never believe it!

They had been husband and wife for twenty years, the model couple in everyone's eyes in the neighborhood. How could Shen Lan betray her?

And those two children she raised; back then the doctor said she couldn't bear children, so Shen Lan had adopted a boy and a girl from outside.

She had raised them since they were little; if they weren't biological mother and children, they were even closer than biological!

How could they be ungrateful wretches?

"Who are you?" Si Rong asked anxiously.

But the earpiece was left with only a burst of dial tones.

Si Rong stood holding the receiver for a long time. The person on the phone just now had said she was her from twenty years in the future.

How could this be possible?

Yet that voice was undeniably, fiercely familiar.

After standing for a long time, the phone made no other strange sounds. Only then did Si Rong, feeling drained of strength, slowly move back to the rattan chair on the balcony.

The rose tea in her mouth suddenly seemed to taste bitter.

The autumn sunset shone in through the floor-to-ceiling windows, making her feel restless and upset.

Her mind was full of that phone call.

Shen Lan could never betray her!

From their campus romance to the loving couple everyone envied now, a single look was enough for them to understand each other's meaning.

The sun slowly slanted westward, and a sense of desolation involuntarily rose from the bottom of her heart.

Just the thought that Shen Lan might betray her made Si Rong's heart begin to sink, and sink further, plummeting into the abyss.

This must be someone trying to trick her, jealous of her current happy life!

Si Rong thought to herself.

Suddenly, she leaned back against the rattan chair and laughed again, talking to herself, her red lips muttering unconsciously, "Even twenty years in the future? If the me from twenty years in the future could call the me right now, then why was there only one minute?"

"Right! It's fake!" As if she had finally found the flaw, she stood up and looked at the phone anew. In the twilight, the phone seemed to carry a certain eerie feeling.

Si Rong looked at the phone and said slowly, "If it's not fake, then dial over again and speak clearly!"

At that moment, the telephone bell rang abruptly.

It scared Si Rong so much she almost fell to the ground.

With mixed fear and suspicion, she got up and stepped forward again to pick up the receiver before the ringing stopped.

"Rongrong, shall I bring you a roast duck from Quanjude after work later? Didn't you say you wanted to eat some a couple of days ago?"

It was Shen Lan's voice.

Si Rong's tense body suddenly relaxed, and her nose felt a bit sore.

That was the night two days ago, when she was leaning in Shen Lan's arms,

resting her slightly cool feet against Shen Lan's lower abdomen.

She had casually mentioned she wanted to eat roast duck.

"Then I'll go buy it right now!" Shen Lan immediately made to get up.

Si Rong pushed him back down into the covers, "I was just saying it casually, I don't need to eat it right away."

"Then I'll definitely buy it back as soon as possible so my Wife can have some."

When Shen Lan said those words, his eyes were full of doting affection.

He was always like this, taking even her inadvertent remarks to heart.

Would a man like this betray her?

Si Rong's heart loosened, and she subconsciously wanted to tell him about the strange phone call she had just received.

But thinking of the bizarre nature of the call, Si Rong decided it was better not to talk about it over the phone.

Wait until Shen Lan came back.

Yes, once he came back, everything would be fine.

She wasn't a very decisive person. In her childhood as the youngest daughter of the family, Si Rong had been sheltered and raised with care.

Later, although her family suffered drastic changes, her husband Shen Lan gradually rose through official ranks and continued to keep her protected under his wing. There would always be someone standing in front of her to shield her from wind and rain.

Soon, the door clicked open.

Si Rong went to greet him.

The one who came back was their daughter, Shen Yuan.

She was a high school senior this year, preparing for the sprint to the college entrance examination.

Most of Si Rong's heart and mind were focused on her, helping her with review and daily life.

Although they had a housekeeper, Aunt Wang, Si Rong personally attended to many aspects of her daughter's life.

A young girl like this, whom Shen Lan had carried back as a tiny bundle and watched grow into the poised young woman she was now...

Would a good girl who always sweetly called her "Mom" really be the ungrateful wretch the phone call described?

"Mom, I'm hungry, when is dinner?"

Shen Yuan hugged her and acted spoiled as usual, and Si Rong froze for a moment before embracing her back.

"Aunt Wang went to buy groceries, we can eat soon."

"Mom made snow pear and white fungus soup, drink a little first."

"Mom is the best! I love Mom the most!"

Si Rong scooped a small bowl of soup for her and watched with a smile as she drank it.

"Oh right, Mom, I want to go to Aaron Kwok's concert on Sunday, can you help me buy a ticket?"

Now the "Four Heavenly Kings" were just rising in popularity, and many girls were infatuated with them, driving the price of a single concert ticket up to over a thousand yuan.

You had to know that in the 1990s, over a thousand yuan could comfortably support an ordinary family for a whole year.

And even with money, ordinary people simply couldn't snap up tickets.

But Si Rong's second oldest brother could.

Back when their family fortunes declined, her second brother, Si Han, seized the opportunity of the 1980s reform and opening up, and in just ten years had become a well-known entrepreneur in Huaiyang County.

Good things that others couldn't get, he could always manage to get.

In the past, Si Rong doted on this youngest daughter and never refused her anything.

But perhaps influenced by today's phone call, for the first time she refused her daughter's request, "You're taking the college entrance exam next year, study hard first."

Shen Yuan immediately became unhappy, rolled her single-fold eyelids, put down her half-drunk bowl of soup, and went back to her bedroom.

Si Rong's smile froze halfway on her face.

The door rang again.

This time, the one who came back was Shen Lan.

The man wore a casual jacket and a pair of gold-rimmed glasses. Although he was already forty-three, his figure was still well-maintained, and his delicate face carried a few more mature and steady vibes than when he was young.

Back then, it was precisely for his good looks that Si Rong had married "down" to him.

---

chapters.title: Ungrateful Children
chapters.content:
"Rongrong, what's wrong?"

As soon as he entered, Shen Lan changed into his slippers, placed the roast duck on the dining table, and immediately sensed her unhappiness.

Hearing his gentle voice, Si Rong felt even more aggrieved.

So she whispered to Shen Lan about what had just happened with Shen Yuan.

"What's the big deal?" Shen Lan smiled and pulled her into his arms, "Asking our second brother to help buy a concert ticket isn't a hard thing. We can just give the money to Second Brother later!"

Shen Lan often said this, but in truth, not a single time had Second Brother ever accepted their money when helping them with tasks.

In the past, Si Rong hadn't thought much of it, but today, hearing it made Si Rong feel rather uncomfortable.

"It's not about buying the ticket, nor is it about the money," Si Rong shared her worries with him. "Xiaoyuan is about to take the college entrance exams. If her mind isn't on her studies, how is she going to get into college?"

Shen Lan rubbed the bridge of his nose.

Si Rong knew this was the precursor to his impatience.

However, this man had great manners and never lost his temper with her.

Si Rong also knew when to stop and stopped nagging.

Although Shen Chi and Shen Yuan were adopted, it was obvious that Shen Lan loved them as if they were his own biological children.

Feeling guilty due to her infertility, Si Rong also treated these two children as her own flesh and blood.

It was just that today, for the first time, she had refused Shen Yuan's request, and she hadn't expected the child to react this way.

Could it really be, as that phone call said, that Shen Yuan was truly an ungrateful wretch?

Right, the phone call.

Si Rong brewed over it for a moment, intending to tell Shen Lan about the strange call she received this afternoon.

"Oh right, this afternoon, I..."

Just as Shen Lan turned around, Si Rong suddenly caught sight of a long black hair on the back of his neck.

In that position, it was impossible to snag one unless there was very intimate contact.

And her own hair had been dyed a chestnut-brown color not long ago.

Si Rong's heart skipped a beat.

"What were you doing this afternoon?" Si Rong asked, suppressing the shock in her heart.

Shen Lan showed not a shred of suspicion as he placed the warmed roast duck onto a plate.

He naturally and mildly told her his itinerary, "I had a meeting, and then attended a ribbon-cutting ceremony for a real estate development."

As a deputy county magistrate, these tasks were commonplace.

For a moment, Si Rong didn't know where she should start doubting.

At that moment, Aunt Wang came back from grocery shopping.

"Sir is back? I was delayed a bit buying groceries, the rice is already steamed, I'll go stir-fry the dishes right now."

After Aunt Wang went into the kitchen, Shen Lan tore off one of the duck legs and handed it to Si Rong.

He dotingly said, "Let me guess what Rongrong was doing all afternoon, did you watch TV first, then take a nap, and finally drink tea on the balcony admiring that jar of new lotus flowers you planted?"

A pang hit Si Rong's heart once more.

Shen Lan was always like this, knowing all her preferences.

"I... I'm going to the restroom."

Once inside the restroom, locking the door behind her, Si Rong still couldn't calm her churning emotions for a while.

What on earth was that hair about?

She remembered that Shen Lan's secretary this year, Xiao Huang, had short hair, and there didn't seem to be any particularly pretty young girls in their office.

Aunt Wang finished cooking and called them to dinner, but Shen Yuan refused to come out of her room to eat.

Si Rong knew she was waiting for her to compromise, just like she always did.

Yet today her mind was in turmoil, and she simply didn't have the heart to coax her.

Shen Lan used a small bowl to scoop up some dishes, along with a roast duck leg, and took them to the bedroom.

Guilt surfaced in Si Rong's heart once again; Shen Lan truly was a good father. If she had been able to bear a child for Shen Lan back then, they wouldn't have had any regrets between them.

After quite a while, when Shen Lan still hadn't come out of their daughter's room, Si Rong pushed the door open to look, only to see Shen Yuan clinging to Shen Lan like a kangaroo, hanging onto him.

Her fluffy hair was draped all the way down to Shen Lan's neck.

Si Rong's expression softened somewhat. It was just her overthinking things, letting that strand of hair throw her off balance.

Whose hair could it be, if not Shen Yuan's?

It was impossible for Shen Lan to be so intimate with any woman other than the two of them.

"All right, come out and eat. Tomorrow I'll have your Second Uncle help you ask about the concert tickets."

Only when Shen Lan said this did Shen Yuan's expression clear up. She immediately turned to hug Si Rong and act spoiled, "Mom! You're the best! Have Second Uncle buy a few more tickets! I want to go with my classmates!"

"Fine! We'll do whatever my little princess wants!"

Since Shen Lan had said so, Si Rong couldn't ruin their fun, so she figured she would just give the money to her second brother later.

As soon as the family sat down to eat, Shen Chi came back, chatting about his work while eating.

"Mom, why don't you have Big Uncle take me under his wing? I also want to start my own foreign trade company and not work for others."

Si Rong's oldest brother, Si Yan, ran a foreign trade company of considerable scale and already drove his own small sedan.

It was one of the first batches of joint-venture cars.

Although Shen Lan, as deputy county magistrate, also had a car for getting around, it belonged to the government and not to him personally.

He could use it for official business, but it was inconvenient for personal matters.

In short, although their family's living standard was already quite good, there was always someone better, a mountain higher than the next.

Compared to the Si family, they still fell a bit short.

Therefore, the siblings Shen Chi and Shen Yuan had been very close to the Si family since childhood.

"Your Big Uncle is busy. I'll mention it to him next time I see him."

Si Rong agreed subconsciously, then remembered the phone call stating that the children were ungrateful wretches.

Would Shen Chi turn out like that?

Perhaps due to her nature, while she also loved Shen Yuan dearly, in the bottom of her heart she favored Shen Chi more.

Shen Chi had a very sweet tongue.

In the past two years as she approached forty and experienced some appearance anxiety, Shen Chi would praise her as the most beautiful mother in the entire world every time he came home.

"Thank you, the most beautiful mother in the whole world!" Shen Chi laughed heartily. "Just wait at home in peace. Later on, when your son makes a big business, I'll definitely take good care of you!"

Si Rong was coaxed into laughter by him.

"Rongrong, eat some fish."

Shen Lan placed fish with the bones meticulously removed into her bowl; a habit Shen Lan had maintained since they first got together.

Yet, for some reason, today Si Rong could not taste the deliciousness of the fish.

After dinner, Aunt Wang washed the dishes, and Shen Lan accompanied her for a walk in the neighborhood as usual.

Aixinjia Garden was housing allocated by the government after Shen Lan became county magistrate. Most of the people living here were Shen Lan's colleagues, either wealthy or noble.

They hadn't walked far when they ran into someone coming the other way, Si Rong's longtime friend, Li Xuan.

She lived right downstairs from them and was still unmarried.

chapters.title: He Loves You Very Much
chapters.content:
The moment Si Rong saw them, Li Xuan smiled and walked over.

"You two are so deeply devoted to each other, it's enough to make anyone envious!"

Knowing Li Xuan was teasing her, Si Rong smiled and shot her a playful, reproachful look.

Right then, Shen Lan ran into a colleague and stepped away to chat.

"I'm going to go chat with Li Xuan," Si Rong told Shen Lan, before pulling Li Xuan along to stroll by the lake in the residential complex.

"Xuanxuan, there's something I want to tell you."

Si Rong trusted Li Xuan deeply. The two of them had been good friends since university.

Over the years, they had accompanied each other through many major milestones.

When Si Rong got married all those years ago, Li Xuan was her bridesmaid.

"Rongrong, what's wrong? You look a bit pale today."

Li Xuan asked with concern.

Si Rong sighed. "Xuanxuan, do you think it's possible that Shen Lan would betray me?"

She didn't miss the flash of astonishment in Li Xuan's eyes.

Look at that! Even her closest friend didn't believe Shen Lan would ever betray her, let alone anyone else.

Li Xuan frowned. "Rongrong, did someone say something to you?"

"Mm."

For reasons of her own, Si Rong didn't mention the phone call from that afternoon to Li Xuan.

She felt as though Xuanxuan might suspect she was losing her mind.

And wouldn't she? Who on earth would believe such a thing if she told them?

Her future self had called her, telling her to divorce her deeply devoted husband and leave behind their ungrateful adoptive son and daughter.

Even she herself was beginning to doubt whether that afternoon phone call had ever truly existed.

Or perhaps some lunatic had dialed her number by mistake.

By now, it was almost driving her crazy too.

"Rongrong, don't just listen to whatever nonsense people spout. I know better than anyone how good Shen Lan is to you. Back in university when those thugs bullied you, he didn't hesitate a second to stand up for you and even took a knife wound; when he found out you couldn't have children, he didn't hesitate a second to insist on marrying you, not caring what anyone else thought. How could a man like that ever betray you?"

"He loves you very much," Li Xuan said with absolute earnestness.

Si Rong knew this.

Yet, there's no smoke without fire.

Even if the phone call from that afternoon wasn't real, it still meant that deep in her subconscious, she suspected Shen Lan might betray her.

Si Rong asked her again, "Then do you think I look old?"

They always said a man at forty is like a blossoming flower, but a woman at forty is like discarded bean curd pulp.

Shen Lan was still brimming with charm, but nowadays when she walked down the street, she no longer turned heads the way she did in her youth.

Young girls kept popping up batch after batch, like bamboo shoots after a spring rain.

Perhaps Shen Lan's mind had wandered, even just for a moment... After years of marriage, the mere thought of this possibility made Si Rong's chest ache with a dull pain.

Everyone said Shen Lan loved her to the marrow of her bones, but she too had been worthy of such love from him.

Back in university, she originally had the chance to go abroad for advanced dance studies, but she stayed in China solely for Shen Lan's sake.

And speaking of their marriage back then, Shen Lan was merely a lowly section chief at the time. If not for her barrenness, why would the Si family have ever agreed to her marrying down?

Her grandfather had been a red capitalist.

Her father, with a background of studying abroad, was a diplomat, and her mother was a translator.

They were one of the most prominent, well-known households in Huaiyang County.

Chatting with Li Xuan hadn't managed to lift Si Rong's spirits.

Soon after, Shen Lan came looking for her, and the two of them headed home.

The night was deep. After washing up, the couple lay down in bed.

Unlike many couples who started sleeping in separate beds by the time they reached forty, the two of them still shared the same pillow to this day.

To the extent that if Shen Lan went on a business trip, Si Rong couldn't even fall asleep on her own.

"Rongrong, is something on your mind?" Shen Lan pulled her into his arms, gently stroking her back. "If you don't want to talk about it, then wait until you're ready. I'll always be right by your side."

Si Rong held him gently, her heart moved to the point of utter ruin.

Perhaps she really was just overthinking things.

It was all that wretched phone call's fault.

Speaking of that phone call, Si Rong suddenly remembered something.

"Shen Lan, I still don't quite know how to use our home telephone," she said.

Si Rong was a natural beauty from the Jiangnan region, and her speaking voice naturally carried the soft, melodious cadence of the southern dialects.

Shen Lan chuckled softly. "Don't worry. If you don't know how to use it, I'll teach you tomorrow."

"Alright. Does our telephone automatically record every single incoming call?" Si Rong asked again.

"Of course. But you can't tell from the phone at home; you have to go down to the paging center to check."

"Where is the paging center?"

Shen Lan used his fingers to gently brush away the stray locks of hair across her forehead. "It's on that small hill at the very north of our county, near the dam."

Si Rong knew that place. She gave a dainty, elegant yawn and slowly closed her eyes, planning to go to the paging center tomorrow to check whether she really had received such a phone call that afternoon.

She couldn't keep letting herself be eaten away by suspicion.

It would end up damaging the affection between her and Shen Lan.

Early the next morning, after Shen Lan left for work and Shen Yuan went off to school, Si Rong tidied herself up simply.

She wore a creamy-white long dress as a base, layered with a khaki cashmere overcoat, and stepped into a pair of soft sheepskin boots.

Although she was approaching forty, because she had never given up dancing and had never borne children, her waist remained slender, graceful, and alluring.

She took the bus all the way to the northern dam of the city.

Si Rong took a deep breath before stepping inside to tell the customer service representative at the paging center that she wanted to check her household's call records from the previous night.

Originally, the paging center refused to let her check, but fortunately, Si Rong ran into an old classmate.

With her help, she managed to look up the telephone records from the previous night.

The records showed only a single call made by Shen Lan from his office unit.

Could that phone call really have been a product of her own imagination?

Si Rong's expression instantly turned grim, especially when she recalled her dream from the night before.

"Could this record possibly have errors?"

Her old classmate smiled faintly. "Of course not."

Ever since elementary school, she had envied Si Rong, and she still did now. Come to think of it, they were women fast approaching forty.

Crow's feet were creeping up the corners of their eyes, and their gazes had grown weathered and worldly after being tempered by the passing years, yet time seemed to treat Si Rong with extraordinary favor.

She had been pretty from childhood to adulthood, pampered by her family in the past, and now held in the palm of her husband's hand. Perhaps this was simply what it meant to be born with good fortune!

After pondering for a moment, Si Rong said, "Lili, could you help me check the call records for Shen Lan's office too?"

That way, she could compare them and see if there was any possibility of errors in the paging center's phone records.

If there were no problems at all, then she probably ought to pay a visit to the hospital's psychiatry department.

"What? Suspecting your husband is playing around behind your back?" Cui Lili rolled her eyes with playful exasperation. "Miss Si Rong, did you enter menopause early?"

Otherwise, why else would she be having these sudden, erratic impulses?

Which of their old classmates didn't know just how utterly doting Shen Lan was toward Si Rong?

You'd have an easier time making people believe Si Rong had been unfaithful than believing Shen Lan would ever cheat.

---

chapters.title: A Familiarly Ringing Number
chapters.content:
"No, I just want to check whether the backend records at your paging center are prone to errors."

Si Rong knew that over the years, Shen Lan had truly lived up to being a good husband, which was why absolutely no one around them believed he would ever betray her.

"Fine!" Cui Lili printed out the call records for Shen Lan's office and handed them over to Si Rong. "My lady, please take a look!"

"Lili, thank you today," Si Rong said sincerely.

Cui Lili turned back around to attend to other customers. "We're old classmates, we don't need to stand on ceremony for this. I won't see you out; let's get together again sometime."

After leaving the paging center, Si Rong opened the small stack of phone records Cui Lili had printed for her.

Since she didn't have a regular job, she paid a great deal of attention to Shen Lan's affairs.

She recognized most of the frequently appearing numbers on these records, but one particular string of digits caught her attention.

The frequency with which it appeared wasn't particularly high.

Once every seven or eight days, appearing four times over the past month or so.

What drew her attention was the exact time these calls were placed: every single one of them was made after 8:00 PM.

The two most recent dates, as Si Rong recalled, were precisely the times when Shen Lan was away on business trips, claiming he had to go to the neighboring county.

She flipped further back and discovered that the other two call logs also roughly coincided with the times Shen Lan was away on business.

The fingers pinching the paper tightened slightly, white marks showing through her pale fingernails.

Today, she had originally come to the paging center to banish her inner demons, but unexpectedly, rather than leaving the old demons behind, she had added a brand-new one.

There was definitely something wrong with this phone call!

Shen Lan kept a telephone directory that recorded almost all of his important contacts.

Yet this number was completely absent from it.

If she hadn't stumbled into printing out the call logs for Shen Lan's office at the paging center today by sheer coincidence.

She would never have known about this phone call at all.

Who on earth was it that made Shen Lan call them every single time before going on a business trip? Was he really just going on business trips?

Without realizing it, Si Rong walked all the way back to her home.

The Si family's commercial empire rose rapidly after the founding of the People's Republic. At its peak, half the households in the southern region ate flour and seasonings produced by the Si family. In 1965, they were slapped with the label of capitalists by competitors, and for a time, when a wall is about to collapse everyone gives it a push.

Later, with the Reform and Opening Up, the two sons of the Si family quickly leveraged their exceptional business acumen to join forces and revitalize the family business once more.

"Young mistress is back!" Aunt Li was overjoyed at the sight of Si Rong. After calling out, a silver-haired woman wearing a deep green wool sweater soon descended the stairs, looking pleasantly surprised.

"Rongrong is back. Your father was just mentioning you a couple of days ago."

Si Rong forced herself to put on a cheerful expression. "Really? Where is Dad?"

"He went out fishing with one of his fishing buddies."

The mother and daughter sat on the sofa chatting for a while, and Mother Si hurriedly instructed Aunt Li to stew snow fungus, bird's nest, and ejiao for the noon meal.

"I feel like your complexion isn't looking too good. You need to nourish yourself. Haven't you been eating well at home these past couple of days?"

Si Rong was long past the age of pouring her heart out to her mother whenever she had a worry. Her mother was seventy-three this year, precisely the age referred to in folk superstition as "seventy-three, eighty-four, a major hurdle in life," and minor ailments had plagued her continuously since the start of the year.

"I've been eating well. Shen Lan even bought me roast duck from Quanjude to eat."

Si Rong sat beside her mother, looking at the wisps of silver hair at her temples, and suddenly felt a sour sting in the bridge of her nose.

All the words she had wanted to pour out instantly vanished back inside.

She was nearly forty years old; she couldn't let her mother worry about her anymore.

After having lunch with her mother at home, Si Rong left.

Her mind was a chaotic mess as she walked along the roadside.

She had a slow-to-warm-up temperament.

Over the years, aside from her family and Shen Lan, she didn't have many people she could truly confide in.

Apart from Li Xuan, the only other residue of her naive university friendships was Ming Zi.

Passing a public telephone booth, she placed a call to Ming Zi, arranging to meet her at the 1991 Cafe.

Back when they graduated from university, Ming Zi had swiftly broken up with her passionate boyfriend and married a second-generation rich kid who had pursued her for a long time.

Si Rong had always remembered what Ming Zi said back then: a woman should marry someone who loves her rather than someone she loves.

At the time, she had simply thought Ming Zi was being realistic.

Yet through all these years, Ming Zi had always lived a very happy life.

Unlike Si Rong marrying down, or Li Xuan's voluntary celibacy, Ming Zi always knew exactly what she wanted.

The cafe was playing a rendition of A Valley Liaison, while Si Rong rested her chin in her hands, gazing out the window.

Soon, Ming Zi floated in wearing a Korean-style dress, taking off her oversized toad-shaped sunglasses upon seeing her.

"Little Princess Si Rong, what instructions does Your Highness have today summoning this humble maid?"

Ming Zi teased.

Back then, the three of them shared a dormitory, and they all knew the extent to which the Si family spoiled this little princess.

Every single week, Mother Si would personally come to the dorm to make her bed for her.

Of course, she would also treat her and Li Xuan to meals, gift them cosmetics that young girls loved, and ask them to take good care of their little princess.

If Si Rong hadn't insisted on living in the dorms, Mother Si would have bought an apartment right next to their school.

After two cups of coffee were served, Ming Zi finally noticed the expression on her face, which was different from her usual demeanor.

"What's wrong? Didn't you find the clothes and shoes you liked? Or is Shen Lan working too busy to keep you company, leaving you too bored?"

These were all the reasons Ming Zi, as a good friend, could imagine for little princess Si Rong to be in a bad mood.

Si Rong had a blessed life, and she was quite simply the girl with the best fortune Ming Zi had ever met.

Not only was she the universally adored darling of her maiden family, but even the minor section chief she had stubbornly insisted on marrying down for had now risen to become the deputy county magistrate.

"Ming Zi, I suspect that Shen Lan might have someone else outside."

Earlier on the road, when she passed the telephone booth, Si Rong had actually considered dialing that number.

After all, nothing had been verified yet.

However, a woman's sixth sense was extremely powerful.

Connecting the dots with various details surrounding Shen Lan's business trips, Si Rong had still sensed that something was amiss.

"What? Shen Lan dares to keep a mistress on the side?" Ming Zi's reaction was different from Li Xuan's; her very first reaction was anger.

Because she knew her friend well enough, Si Rong wasn't the kind of person to let her pampered status go to her head or chase shadows based on baseless rumors.

Unless there was evidence.

"What? Did you see the mistress?"

Si Rong shook her head. Looking at Ming Zi, she felt a surge of gratitude; grateful that she hadn't like Li Xuan, who questioned her and chose to believe Shen Lan instead.

"It's just that, by sheer coincidence, I checked the phone bill for Shen Lan's office." Si Rong showed her the printed sheet from her handbag.

"It's this call right here."

Ming Zi's almond-shaped eyes narrowed slightly as she carefully examined the call Si Rong was pointing to. "Si Rong, why do I feel like this number looks a bit familiar?"

"You've seen it?" Si Rong asked.

chapters.title: Do Not Alert the Enemy
chapters.content:
Mingzi looked again, viewing it from different angles, and began to doubt her own eyes. "It does look a bit familiar. I must have seen it somewhere before."

Perhaps it was by chance, but try as she might, she couldn't recall.

"Rongrong, what are your plans?"

Mingzi's heart ached for her. Ever since they met in college, Si Rong had been like a little princess in her eyes.

She had envied her, but never felt jealous.

That was because Si Rong was genuinely a good girl. Out of the three of them in the dorm, only Si Rong came from the most modest background. Hailing from a rural area, her family could barely scrape together her tuition, let alone help with living expenses.

Every time they went to eat, Si Rong would always ask her to come along, because the portions sent by her family's servants always had an extra share.

Not just her, even Li Xuan had shared many of those meals.

If not for Si Rong, she wouldn't have known how she survived those four years of college.

No one ever brought up these kindnesses, but Mingzi always remembered them.

Such a good girl, and that bastard Shen Lan actually dared to do something to wrong her?

Although her own second-generation-wealth husband also kept women on the side, it was different.

Back then, she had married her wealthy husband purely for his good family background, and she had long been prepared for the fact that he wouldn't be devoted to her for life.

So over the years, as her husband kept mistresses outside, she turned a blind eye, focusing all her energy on raising her children and keeping control of the majority of her husband's assets.

But Si Rong was different.

As the little princess of the Si family, she had had so many outstanding suitors back then, yet Shen Lan was merely a mediocre one among them.

If not for all the benefits he reaped from the Si family, could he have climbed to his current position as deputy county magistrate?

Now that he had money and power, he wanted to play fancy games?

Si Rong was a year younger than her, and now she was almost forty.

Mingzi looked at Si Rong's bewildered, shaking head, and a fresh wave of heartache washed over her.

She pulled Si Rong to lean on her shoulder and comforted her, "It's fine. Whatever you want to do, I'll help you."

Tearing down the mistress? She was on it!

Cursing out Shen Lan? She was on it too!

Whatever Si Rong pointed at, she would attack!

"I want to find out who that woman is."

Si Rong thought for a long time. "Once I figure all this out, I'll divorce Shen Lan."

Mingzi was deeply shocked inwardly, but she understood. Si Rong and Shen Lan had truly loved each other, and she had never tolerated any flaws in her relationships; choosing to divorce was a normal reaction.

However, with Shen Lan now a deputy county magistrate thanks to the Si family's support, if Si Rong just divorced him like that, it would let that mistress off too lightly.

"Right! Let's find out where that shameless woman lives! Then you stand aside, and I'll go up, scratch her face, pull out her teeth, and rip her hair out bald! Let's see how she dares to seduce men again after that!"

Mingzi was very familiar with this routine. Whenever her husband wanted to get rid of a mistress, he would condone her making a scene like this, and no matter how clingy the mistress was, she wouldn't dare pester him anymore.

Si Rong: ...

She hadn't really thought of doing it that way, but it sounded awfully satisfying.

"By the way, are you going to tell Li Xuan about this?" Mingzi asked again.

The friendship among the three of them had lasted until now entirely because of Si Rong.

In her view, over the years Li Xuan had received just as much care from Si Rong as she had, so Li Xuan should charge into battle for Si Rong just like her whenever she needed them.

"Better... not."

At the thought of Li Xuan's profession, Si Rong said, "She's a teacher and has always cared about her reputation. It's better not to tell her about this kind of thing!"

Besides, yesterday when she was only harboring suspicions, Li Xuan's reaction had made her feel rather uncomfortable.

Like everyone else, Li Xuan was dead certain that Shen Lan would never cheat.

She preferred Mingzi's reaction.

Unconditional trust and favoritism toward her.

"I'm wondering, should I call that number back?"

Si Rong felt both heartbroken and immensely curious, scratching her head in suspense. What kind of girl could Shen Lan have taken a fancy to?

Younger than her? Or prettier?

"Not yet," Mingzi advised her. "If you do that, you'll alert the enemy."

"Was it Cui Lili who helped you look up this phone record?"

Si Rong nodded.

"I wonder if she can check the installation address for this phone number."

Si Rong shook her head. "Not yet. If Cui Lili finds out, probably all our classmates will know."

She still clung to a sliver of wishful thinking; perhaps this was all just a misunderstanding.

The phone call was a figment of her imagination, a blunder, and the number was just for official business.

"Then here's what we do: we lie low for now. The next time Shen Lan goes on a business trip, we'll follow him and catch the turtle in the jar!"

Mingzi felt this was the best approach for now.

"But Shen Lan's business trips aren't fixed," Si Rong frowned. Moreover, during this time, she didn't even know how to face Shen Lan.

Waiting was an agonizing process; from yesterday to today, she had already suffered enough just waiting.

Yet she couldn't think of a better way either.

Today was Sunday, and Shen Yuan was coming home early from school.

That child was impatient and would definitely ask her about the concert tickets.

Si Rong didn't want to go home; she felt entirely overwhelmed and annoyed.

"Mingzi, do you think an adopted child can ever truly be raised to be close to you?"

Si Rong cupped her chin in her hands, recalling the phone call from yesterday evening once more.

That voice had been somewhat hoarse, filled with heartbreak and absolute despair.

"Hard to say," Mingzi had three children of her own, two boys and a girl. "You treat others with sincerity, and they'll do the same. Don't worry, Shen Chi and Shen Yuan were raised by you personally since they were so little; they're no different from biological ones."

She had seen with her own eyes how deeply Si Rong loved those two children.

To be honest, Si Rong worried no less than she did as a biological mother.

The instance she remembered most vividly was when Shen Chi had meningitis and was at death's door while Shen Lan was busy with work. It was Si Rong who stayed with her at the hospital, keeping watch by the child's side all night without closing her eyes.

When Shen Yuan was little and almost snatched away by child abductors while out with her grandmother, it was Si Rong who begged the two elders of the Si family to pull strings and seal off all major traffic arteries in Huaiyang City until the child was found.

Si Rong used to think the same way, but now she couldn't quite bring herself to believe it.

After chatting with Mingzi for a long time, as they parted ways, Mingzi told her that if staying at home felt too painful, she could come and stay at her house for a while.

Si Rong was thinking the same thing.

Mingzi had even thought of the excuse for her: she would just say that Mingzi's husband had strayed again, and she was feeling heartbroken and needed company.

She repeatedly urged Si Rong not to alert the enemy just yet.

Yet on her way back, passing by a public phone booth, all of Mingzi's warnings were thrown to the wind by Si Rong.

Comparing it against the string of digits, she dropped a one-yuan coin into the slot and dialed the number.

---

chapters.title: The Campus Male God of Student Days
chapters.content:
Because she was too nervous, Si Rong felt her fingers trembling slightly.

After a few rings on the other end, a voice came through: "Hello?"

"Hello?"

It was a woman's voice.

Shen Lan really had betrayed her!

Because she frequently made calls to Shen Lan's office, she knew this voice did not belong to any female staff member in his office.

With a heavy heart and complete turmoil, Si Rong hung up the phone.

Tears fell helplessly.

For a moment, she had no idea what she should do.

So every time Shen Lan went on a business trip, he was with another woman?

The blow was too heavy; Si Rong had never imagined that Shen Lan would be with someone else.

Leaning against the phone booth for a long time, Si Rong finally walked out in a daze.

Her mind was a chaotic mess...

One moment she wondered when Shen Lan had betrayed her, was it recently, or even earlier?

Remembering how she used to scoff at the "seven-year itch" in marriages when she was young, she thought what a fool she truly was.

Actually, what was the point of all this?

She wasn't the kind of person to cling bitterly; if Shen Lan had fallen for someone else, he could have just made it clear to her. She might have been hurt, but the pain would only last a while, and then they could divorce and each start a new life.

Finding a mistress outside, how sordid and disgusting!

She had always believed their love was different from others.

For all these years, although she had grown accustomed to Mingzi's husband keeping mistresses left and right, she had always thought Shen Lan would be that one exception.

Turns out, he wasn't at all.

Taking advantage of the early hour, Si Rong decided to take the bus home, pack a few clothes, and move into Mingzi's place as she had suggested.

She didn't want to see Shen Lan right now.

Aunt Wang was simmering chicken soup and smiled upon seeing her return, "Madam, Miss loves my home-raised chicken soup the most. Would you like to taste it first?"

Madam always paid attention to these matters.

The "Miss" she referred to was naturally Shen Yuan.

Yet today, Si Rong simply walked past her with an indifferent expression and headed straight to the bedroom.

Si Rong sat on the Simmons mattress, staring blankly at the intimate framed photo of her and Shen Lan on the bedside table.

Shen Lan's profile was gentle and jade-like, smiling as he looked back at her.

Was it fake?

As she packed her clothes, she recalled the mysterious phone call.

The fact that Shen Lan had betrayed her was practically confirmed. So were Shen Chi and Shen Yuan really going to turn out to be ungrateful wretches as well?

She was unwilling to believe it.

After all, those two were children she had raised with her own hands; she had poured even more effort into them than Shen Lan had.

The caller had also mentioned a third thing: to buy as many properties as possible.

Si Rong took the savings passbooks out of their safe.

Perhaps because she had never really lacked money since she was a little girl, Si Rong had never paid much attention to such things.

Married for twenty years, she had rarely cared about how much money was in their passbooks.

Anyway, the drawer always had an inexhaustible supply of cash left by Shen Lan for her to spend.

When she visited her maiden home, her father, mother, and two older brothers still treated her like a child, stuffing money into her bag.

There were two passbooks: one had over ninety thousand yuan, and the other had thirteen thousand.

She packed them into her bag; buying property was the only thing she could do now.

If that phone call truly came from her future self, Si Rong chose to believe it.

However, because Mingzi had self-studied law, reportedly to ensure her three children wouldn't get the short end of the stick in the future, Si Rong had also picked up some knowledge in this area.

This money belonged to the marital property shared by her and Shen Lan; even buying a house would still belong to both of them.

She should consult Mingzi before buying.

Just as she finished packing, the telephone in the living room rang.

At this hour, it was most likely Shen Lan. Si Rong heard Aunt Wang running over to pick it up.

"Madam is in the bedroom."

"Alright, I will relay the message to Madam."

Si Rong walked out carrying her small suitcase, and Aunt Wang looked rather surprised, "Madam, are you going out?"

"Yes, tell Sir that I've gone to Mingzi's house."

Aunt Wang nodded, "Very well, Madam. Sir just called earlier to say he'll be working a bit late tonight."

"Understood."

Si Rong knew how many personnel changes there would be in Huaiyang City's leadership team before the New Year; she had heard the county magistrate was transferring to the city, leaving the magistrate's position vacant.

Shen Lan was busy campaigning, but he wasn't the only one eyeing that position.

So he would be very busy during this time.

"But, what about Miss later..." Aunt Wang wanted to ask if Madam was just going to leave like this and ignore Miss, but before she could finish, Si Rong had already pulled her suitcase away.

Their house wasn't far from Mingzi's.

To please her mother-in-law, Mingzi still lived with her three children in the steel factory's family quarters.

However, their place was quite spacious, and Mingzi's mother-in-law was considered fairly easy to get along with.

When Si Rong arrived, Mingzi was waiting for her right at the entrance of the residential compound.

Taking the suitcase from her hand, Mingzi said, "Let's go! You're sleeping with me tonight."

Hearing those words, Si Rong knew her husband wouldn't be coming home tonight either.

Sigh! It seemed it was always women who were left waiting bitterly.

Just as they entered the courtyard, they bumped straight into someone.

A man in a stand-collar military uniform stood beside a military jeep, his sharply defined features dusted with frost, exuding the cold, piercing aura of a high-altitude flower.

Jiang Cheng.

As dazzling as he had been back in their campus days.

Back then, many people on campus secretly held a crush on Jiang Cheng; he was like a male god.

In the blink of an eye, they were already nearing forty.

Time truly flew by!

She hadn't expected to run into Jiang Cheng here, and her eyes were still red and swollen.

Though perhaps Jiang Cheng no longer remembered her at all.

Si Rong lowered her gaze, walking past Jiang Cheng alongside Mingzi, and then heard the sound of the jeep door closing followed by it driving away.

Indeed, he certainly wouldn't remember; wouldn't remember that they were once old classmates.

"Did you know?" Mingzi linked her arm with hers. "Jiang Cheng was just transferred back to our Huaiyang Military Region this year, and I heard he's already a division commander. By the way, I heard he only brought a daughter back with him this time, and everyone in the compound is guessing he's divorced. Back in school, everyone used to say he liked you."

"Don't talk nonsense," Si Rong didn't believe she had that kind of charm, and besides, she had no mood to reminisce right now.

"It's true. I heard he even wrote you a love letter back then."

Si Rong was somewhat speechless, "That's just gossip! I never received any love letter from Jiang Cheng."

Such an arrogant male god writing a love letter to her?

"But during our last class reunion, I heard Cui Lili mention that Jiang Cheng had someone deliver a love letter to you."

Yet Si Rong had no recollection of it whatsoever.

"No? Cui Lili spoke with such conviction. But I wonder who Jiang Cheng could have entrusted to bring that love letter to you?"

Back in their student days, even if someone entrusted another, they wouldn't choose someone who had nothing to do with the girl. At that time, she, Li Xuan, and Si Rong were the closest of friends.

"I'll ask Li Xuan about it next time I see her."

Mingzi pushed open the door for Si Rong to enter, then seemed to remember something, "Oh right, Li Xuan seems to have a boyfriend. Did she tell you?"

Normally, she wouldn't ask Li Xuan about such things directly.

They always said friendships of three were a bit crowded; among the three of them, she only hung out with Li Xuan because of Si Rong.

chapters.title: Just Want to Leave
chapters.content:
Si Rong sat down on the sofa, shook her head, and at the same time looked somewhat surprised. "Has she finally figured things out?"

After graduating from university, she and Ming Zi married one after another, leaving only Li Xuan remaining single.

She always seemed entirely uninterested in men.

Now pushing forty, had she finally come to her senses?

"I think something's fishy," Ming Zi first brewed a pot of tribute chrysanthemum tea for Si Rong. "The last time I passed by your neighborhood, I remembered I didn't bring my wallet and planned to look for you to borrow some money. But nobody was home, so I went to Li Xuan's place instead. Guess what I saw the moment I walked in?"

"What?"

Si Rong asked with curiosity.

"A man's shoes. Didn't Li Xuan sever ties with her son-preferring parents early on and have nothing to do with them? So those couldn't belong to any family member of hers."

"The most suggestive part was Li Xuan's reaction," Ming Zi guessed. "Her eyes were panicked when I saw those shoes, as if she was terrified I'd figure something out."

"If they were normal dating partners, why would she be so secretive with me? She could have introduced him quite openly. So my guess is that whoever she's seeing right now must not be fit to see the light of day."

Si Rong wasn't so sure. "Li Xuan has a strong and proud disposition; perhaps you've misunderstood her."

After all, the two of them frequently bickered. Maybe Li Xuan was just worried she'd be mocked by Ming Zi for dating at her age and therefore chose to keep quiet.

"Maybe," Ming Zi knew Si Rong regarded Li Xuan as a friend in her heart, so she didn't say any more. Still, she always felt that with a person like Li Xuan, she might well be a mistress.

Back when they shared a dorm, Ming Zi had once caught Li Xuan reporting a girl who was competing with her for a scholarship, and only after that did the scholarship end up going to Li Xuan.

That girl was directly expelled from school.

Later on, however, Ming Zi found out that the girl's so-called two-timing was actually engineered behind the scenes by Li Xuan.

Anyway, that person had character issues.

She was incapable of doing anything good.

For dinner, Ming Zi's three children were not eating at home, and her mother-in-law practiced a wellness routine of eating no food past noon, so Ming Zi personally cooked dinner for the two of them.

She stir-fried a plate of garlic and spicy crayfish.

After the oil was hot, she added oil and small millet peppers to release the aroma, tossed in the crayfish, and then added seasonings and half a bottle of beer to simmer for fifteen minutes.

The fragrance of the crayfish wafted out.

She also stir-fried a simple braised beef shank, served with shredded cucumber and shredded carrots.

"Your culinary skills are getting better and better!"

Si Rong tasted a shrimp handed over by Ming Zi and praised.

"Right? No choice, when you're brilliant, you learn everything fast."

Ming Zi narcissistically declared.

Seeing the slight twitch at the corner of Si Rong's mouth, the gloom in her own heart lifted somewhat as well.

Past forty years of age, having a bosom friend was a very lucky thing.

"By the way, I want to ask you, during a marriage, how can you buy a house so that it belongs solely to yourself?"

Ming Zi raised an eyebrow. "You're going to buy a house?"

Si Rong nodded.

It was Shen Lan who had wronged her first. Before getting a divorce, she always had to think more of herself.

"Time is truly cruel; even the little princess is starting to grow scheming."

Ming Zi had studied marriage law for several years, so she quickly came up with a method for her.

"Buy the house in the names of your uncle and aunt, and then have them make a will stating that this property is gifted exclusively to you."

Si Rong nodded. "Alright, accompany me to look at houses tomorrow!"

Ming Zi nodded, feeling a pang of heartache.

Why were men all so cheap? Always loving the new and abandoning the old.

Dammed Shen Lan!

Although Si Rong looked calm enough on the surface right now, Ming Zi knew her heart must be bleeding.

Twenty years of marriage.

The crayfish portion was a bit too large, and Ming Zi's gossipy heart had nowhere to rest. "Shall we call Li Xuan over to eat with us?"

"Mm."

Ming Zi added, "Better not tell her about you and Shen Lan just yet; she always likes to laugh at people behind their backs."

Soon, Li Xuan arrived.

The three of them sat around together.

Ming Zi placed a bottle of beer in front of each of them.

"Today the three of us are going to have a good get-together."

Half a bottle of beer down, Ming Zi asked, "Li Xuan, aren't you going to introduce your boyfriend to us?"

"What boyfriend?" Li Xuan shook her head, looked at Si Rong, and smiled. "I'll probably be single for the rest of my life!"

She rolled her eyes at Ming Zi. "Those men's leather shoes you saw at my doorway last time belonged to the parent of a student who came to my house for tutoring."

This explanation had no flaws whatsoever, and was even completely perfect.

Li Xuan was a dance teacher at an art school in Huaiyang, with a respectable job, a stable income, and was deeply loved by her students.

"That student's parent must be quite wealthy; he wore Derby shoes, which I remember aren't cheap. There's only one shoe store in our county seat that sells them, Si Rong, don't you always buy Shen Lan's shoes at that store?"

Li Xuan's complexion turned pale for a moment. "I see you're drunk!"

"Alright, let's eat first."

Si Rong mediated. These two had been bickering since their youth all the way toward old age, still acting just like children.

After dinner, Li Xuan found an excuse and left.

"You too, why do you always pick a fight with her? If she didn't want to talk about it, maybe she felt the time wasn't right yet."

Si Rong felt that every time Ming Zi bickered with Li Xuan, Ming Zi's own mood didn't turn out any better.

"I just wanted to peel off her hypocritical mask. Putting on airs the whole day, even telling classmates at a class reunion that I was a gold-digger. She wishes she could dig, could she even find anyone to dig from?"

So it was because of this.

Si Rong tidied up the dining table simply, then helped Ming Zi into the bedroom.

"Alright, you really drank quite a lot today, let's rest."

Ming Zi turned around and hugged Si Rong. "Why don't you just follow my lead and not divorce Shen Lan for now? Right now he's leveraged your Si family's influence to become the deputy county magistrate. The moment you divorce, that mistress will step up and pick up such a huge bargain for free."

"Just drag it out and don't divorce, occupy your position as the magistrate's wife, and treat Shen Lan as a long-term laborer who earns money."

Knowing she meant well for her, Si Rong stroked her face. "Xiao Zi, I'm not like you."

If it was as said over the phone, Shen Chen and Shen Yuan were both ungrateful ingrates, then continuing this marriage of hers would be a joke.

She was already thirty-nine this year; she didn't want the rest of her life to be spent staring in mutual loathing with someone who betrayed her every single day.

When she loved, she loved bravely; when she stopped loving, she could also withdraw at any time.

"I am not as brave or as strong as you; right now, I just want to leave Shen Lan."

Before that, she had only one obsession left: to see what kind of woman was tangled up with Shen Lan.

"Right, I suddenly thought of someone."

Ming Zi pulled open the bedside drawer. "Don't you want to know who the woman fooling around with Shen Lan is? Actually, you don't have to wait for Shen Lan to go on a business trip. This person is called Sun Qiang, and he can help you track down that woman."

---

chapters.title: Investigating Shen Lan
chapters.content:
Actually, Ming Zi had first gotten to know Sun Qiang back when she was young.

At that time, she had just married Luo Sheng and wanted to live a good life with him for the rest of her days.

Unfortunately, less than half a year later, just as she became pregnant, Luo Sheng started looking for other women outside.

She racked her brains, desperately wanting to know what kind of woman Luo Sheng had found.

And so she found Sun Qiang.

Si Rong stroked that string of numbers. "Alright, have him investigate!"

She hadn't been thinking about how to make things difficult for that woman.

It takes two hands to clap, and the greater fault lay with Shen Lan.

Just as the two of them had washed up and were preparing for bed, the phone rang.

"That dog Luo Sheng never calls home when he stays out overnight; it must be Shen Lan!"

One had to admit that this Shen Lan was quite a piece of work.

Other men who cheated would find their nagging, yellow-faced wives at home utterly repulsive in every way.

Not Shen Lan. Every time Si Rong spent the night at her house, Shen Lan would call.

In meticulous detail, he would remind Si Rong not to kick off the quilt at night, not to let his Rongrong sleep on the outer edge, and so forth.

If Si Rong hadn't said it herself, she would never have imagined that a model husband like Shen Lan could have a woman outside.

"I don't want to talk to him."

Si Rong shook her head. Right now, hearing anything at all about Shen Lan made her emotionally repulsed.

Ming Zi went to answer the phone.

"Magistrate Shen, what can I do for you?"

"Rong Rong just went to the bathroom."

"I know, warm up some fresh milk for her before bed, she's sleeping on the inner side, I'm sleeping on the outer side. Alright, alright, hang up!"

When she returned to the bedroom, she saw tears streaming down the corners of Si Rong's eyes.

At that moment, she could understand Si Rong.

If a cheating husband committed domestic violence, hurled insults, and treated his wife in the worst possible way, then the wife would only be happy to leave him and exact revenge.

The hardest part was someone like Shen Lan. He had a woman outside, but he still treated his wife at home exceedingly well.

Much like an ancient emperor with three thousand beauties in his harem, as long as the benefits and affection were given sufficiently, harmonious coexistence was entirely possible.

How would Si Rong choose?

Meanwhile.

The door of the Shen residence was knocked upon. When Shen Lan opened the door and saw who it was, the normally composed and self-contained man's gaze turned frosty.

Then he promptly pushed the woman out, shoving her all the way into the hallway.

"What are you doing here?"

Pushed off balance by him, Li Xuan almost fell.

Between Si Rong's conjecture yesterday and the pair of shoes Ming Zi mentioned today,

Li Xuan felt that today's plate of crayfish was a veritable Feast at Goose Gate.

Or perhaps it was a warning, Ming Zi wanting to warn her not to set her sights on Shen Lan.

Seeing Shen Lan remain silent, she anxiously pursued, "When do you plan to show your hand and divorce her?"

Shen Lan frowned. "What nonsense are you uttering? This is the critical moment for my election as county magistrate. If any mishap occurs, don't ever think about becoming Mrs. Shen in broad daylight!"

"Heh~" Seeing his attitude so vile, Li Xuan sneered, "Magistrate Shen, do you need me to remind you of our agreement back then?"

Shen Lan turned around. The agreement back then...

"Have a little more patience, wait until after the magistrate election, and I'll find a chance to show my hand to her."

"Wait? Of course I'll wait," Li Xuan's eyes were a patch of utter desolation. "Otherwise, what have I been doing all these years."

"You shouldn't feel wronged either. It's not just waiting for me; there's also Chen'er and Yuan'er. They are facing an important turning point in their lives right now. If we lose the backing of the Si family, what will happen in the future? Do you want the children to grow up to be as mediocre and incompetent as us?"

Mediocre.

This was the word Li Xuan detested the most.

She was born in an ordinary small town with three older brothers above her. Originally her parents hadn't planned to have any more, and conceiving her was merely an accident.

Her appearance was ordinary, the love she received was ordinary, everything was so ordinary, as if her very existence was dispensable.

Therefore, the first time she saw Si Rong, she was utterly shocked.

On the first day reporting to the dorm, unlike herself who was entirely alone, Si Rong's parents, grandparents, and two older brothers had all turned out in full force.

She shone like a little princess.

With striking looks and family background.

The other girl in the dorm, Ming Zi, though from an impoverished background, frequently appeared at the center of classmates' topics simply because she possessed a pretty face.

Only she remained completely ignored.

Now, she absolutely would not let her children be as mediocre as she was.

Her goal was nearly within reach; she must absolutely not expose her foot now.

"A-Lan, I believe you."

And I believe in our agreement.

Soon, she would possess everything Si Rong had, becoming the focal point where everyone's gaze converged.

...

The first ray of morning sunlight shone in. Si Rong stretched her back, feeling her eyes somewhat swollen and sore; she had no idea when she'd even fallen asleep last night.

"Get up, let's go out for breakfast!"

Ming Zi had already meticulously planned out their entire day's itinerary in her heart.

She would never give Princess Si any time to be sad.

After they washed up, Ming Zi called Sun Qiang and arranged a place to meet.

Then they headed downstairs for breakfast.

Two bowls of shrimp wontons, and a steamer basket of three-delicacy stuffed mini steamed buns.

Si Rong originally had no appetite to eat, but Ming Zi said if she didn't eat, she wouldn't take her to see the detective later.

"Is he really as miraculous as you say?"

Si Rong was somewhat skeptical.

"You'll know once you see him later."

Sun Qiang was, how should one put it? The kind of person whose face you would quickly forget after a single glance, or rather, someone entirely devoid of memorable features.

"Your husband acting up again?"

Sun Qiang asked familiarly.

"Never mind that piece of trash today; we'd like to ask you to investigate someone else instead."

Sun Qiang's gaze swept over Si Rong before nodding.

Upon learning that the person they wanted him to investigate was Shen Lan, Sun Qiang's eyes widened instantly. "Magistrate Shen?"

"Yes, it's him."

"You want to investigate Magistrate Shen?"

"Right, name your price." Ming Zi didn't elaborate further.

Sun Qiang had heard of this deputy magistrate's fine reputation.

"Two hundred yuan deposit, and the remaining three hundred yuan balance settled after you get the results."

Si Rong drew two hundred-yuan bills from her bag and handed them to him.

Her heart was filled with desolation; never had she imagined that one day she would actually spend money to investigate Shen Lan's private life.

The eighteenth year of their being together was actually going to end in such squalor.

"Alright, how long will it take?"

"About two days."

Si Rong's heart suddenly steadied.

In two days, everything would settle into dust.

After parting ways with Sun Qiang, Si Rong and Ming Zi went to look at houses.

A newly opened real estate project in Huaiyang: Waterside Garden.

Housing prices were nine hundred per square meter.

Housing prices had skyrocketed over the past two years, and many people were still watching and waiting, hoping for housing prices to drop before buying.

Following the sales agent to look at some relatively classic apartment layouts, Si Rong's gaze fell upon those commercial storefront properties at the residential compound's entrance.

Telling her to buy a house over the phone was probably because property values would rise; those street-front shops where businesses could be opened would definitely hold more value; this was Si Rong's own interpretation.

She pointed at the row along the street of Waterside Residential Compound. "I'd like to take a look at these storefront properties."

"You really have a discerning eye, Madam. The layouts of these storefront properties have great investment value. I'll take you to see them right now."

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.content:
There were a total of ten commercial townhouses lining the street, each consisting of an upper and lower floor.

"Are none of them sold yet?"

The saleswoman was quite articulate. "We've had many people come to view them, but no contracts signed yet."

The commercial houses were priced at over eleven hundred per square meter. Si Rong mentally calculated the money she had on hand. "Then I'll take three."

The saleswoman's mouth opened wide enough to fit an egg.

She could tell these two were wealthy madams, but she hadn't expected them to be so boldly extravagant.

Buying three houses in one breath!

It was easier and simpler for her than buying three pieces of clothing.

Following Ming Zi's suggestion, Si Rong went back to her parents' home and mentioned that she wanted to put the newly purchased houses in her parents' names.

Naturally, Si Mother agreed.

She hoped her daughter would have a happy marriage, but of course, she hoped even more that her daughter's happiness wouldn't depend solely on marriage.

After the houses were purchased, before Si Rong could even bring it up, her parents had already drawn up their wills, designating all three commercial houses to belong exclusively to their daughter.

After buying the properties, Si Rong only had a few thousand yuan left in her hands.

The two days passed by in a flash.

Sun Qiang contacted Ming Zi, arranging for them to meet at the cafe where they had seen each other last time, bright and early the next morning.

Si Rong lay in bed with a heavy heart.

She both longed for the clear, definitive outcome after the meeting and feared it at the same time.

She feared she wouldn't be able to bear it, feared she might go crazy.

The telephone rang once more; it was a call from the Shen household.

After answering, Ming Zi mouthed to her that it was her mother-in-law, Mother Shen.

Mother Shen was a single mother, which hadn't been easy.

When Shen Lan was six years old, his father had passed away in an accident.

He had once complained to Si Rong while drunk about the hardships of growing up, how the widow and orphan suffered all kinds of humiliation in the village, making them wise to the ways of the world at an early age.

Therefore, Si Rong understood all too well the crucial status his mother and younger sister held in his heart, and she hadn't skimping on helping them out over the years.

"Xiao Rong, it's so late, why aren't you back yet? I've been sitting on a train all day, hurry back and soak my feet!" Mother Shen's tone was full of dissatisfaction toward Si Rong.

Her son had worked hard outside all day; coming home to find his wife not even there to wait on him; it was simply too lacking in common sense.

If not for her son, could Si Rong be living such a good life today?

"Oh, and as for your younger sister, find her another blind date. That last fellow was absolute trash!"

Mother Shen commanded.

Si Rong fell silent for a moment before simply lying that the signal was bad and hanging up.

She was in no mood to wait on that mother-daughter pair right now.

Mother Shen always put on airs as a mother-in-law in front of her, keeping her under thumb so she could go back to the village and boast to her relatives about how a capitalist's daughter had to wait on her hand and foot.

As for Shen Lan's younger sister, ever since Shen Lan started sending money home, she had stuffed herself until she was round and bloated, and now, well past thirty, she still hadn't managed to get married.

She was another person with ambitions higher than the heavens and a fate thinner than paper.

Back when she first got married, she had sincerely filial piety toward Mother Shen and treated Shen Yun like her own younger sister.

Yet not all sincerity could be exchanged in kind.

Over the past eighteen years, if not for Shen Lan, none of these people would ever have appeared in her life.

"Your mother-in-law is acting up again?"

Si Rong nodded. "She won't be for much longer."

"Are you really sure you want a divorce?" Ming Zi asked. Although Sun Qiang hadn't been convenient to go into detail over the phone today, judging by those couple of remarks, it was certain that Shen Lan had another woman outside.

"Mmm, once I get the evidence of his infidelity tomorrow, I'll lay my cards on the table and divorce him," Si Rong said.

"You're just going to let him off that easily?"

Ming Zi felt it was letting the scumbag get off too cheaply. "If you really want to make a fuss, his official career will be effectively over."

"Let's just part on good terms!"

Si Rong didn't want to burn all her bridges, if only for the sake of the genuine love they once shared.

From now on, each would take their own side of the wide road.

They were both nearing forty; how many days and nights were left in this lifetime? She didn't want to waste her time on such matters.

It wasn't until the next day, upon meeting Sun Qiang, that Si Rong completely changed her mind.

"Ms. Si, I have thoroughly investigated the woman who has been having an overly intimate relationship with your husband. Her name is Li Xuan, and she lives at..."

As soon as he spoke that name, Si Rong's emotions slipped out of her control. She stood up so abruptly that her chair made a loud scraping sound. "Impossible!"

As an outsider, Sun Qiang had already anticipated Si Rong's reaction.

Because he had seen too many cases like this.

If a husband cheating with a random stranger had a damage value of one hundred, then cheating with a best friend multiplied that damage by ten.

And as far as he knew, Ms. Si and that woman were alumni with a friendship spanning twenty years.

Their relationship had been on the verge of turning into familial bonds.

Ms. Si could be said to have suffered a double betrayal from the people closest to her.

That was why he hadn't mentioned it over the phone last night.

"Impossible! How could it..."

Si Rong refused to believe that her husband, Shen Lan, could have gotten together with her good friend Li Xuan right under her nose.

Since when?

"Rongrong," Ming Zi supported her arm, "Calm down first, let's sit down and hear what Sun Qiang has to say."

Tears silently slipped down. Si Rong bit her lip and sat back down.

Sun Qiang continued, "As far as I've been able to track, it started five years ago; around the time that woman moved into your residential compound."

Five years ago, Si Rong naturally remembered.

Back then, she had been very happy, even running over to ask Li Xuan if she had enough money.

Thinking that her friend was single, having her live downstairs from them would at least mean they could look out for one another.

She never imagined she was helping to look after her own husband right into her bed.

How utterly laughable!

Someone who had lived forty years without knowing what hatred felt like suddenly understood it at this moment.

She hated them so much!

After marriage, she had supported her husband's career and tended to the household; Si Rong considered herself a qualified wife.

When friends encountered difficulties, she had helped them with all her might, never distancing herself because of what others said about their flaws; Si Rong considered herself a qualified friend.

Yet why? By what right did these two people betray her?

This caused her far more pain than if Shen Lan had cheated with some casual stranger.

It started five years ago?

Then over these past five years, had these two been whispering sweet nothings to each other every single day right where she couldn't see?

Playing her around in circles like a complete fool?

Si Rong felt her entire worldview had suffered a devastating blow.

In that instant, all malice surged into her heart.

She was going to retaliate! She would pay back every single bit of this pain and deceit in full!

---

chapters.title: Finding a Match for the Younger Sister
chapters.content:
Outwardly, she was completely calm and composed, but no one knew the turbulent waves raging inside her heart.

She had no idea when Sun Qiang left.

It wasn't until Ming Zi beside her suddenly stood up that Si Rong snapped back to her senses and grabbed her arm.

"I'm going to go slap that bitch to death!" Ming Zi said.

"Don't be impulsive," Si Rong pulled her back down. "I want them to regret everything they've done, and live in perpetual misery."

For these two to deceive her, just giving them a few slaps would let them off far too lightly.

Ming Zi blinked, then sat back down beside Si Rong.

"What do you want to do?"

The once-naive little princess had finally been forced to grow up by those two filthy creatures.

"First, we hold our ground, and then..."

---

Si Rong was not going to divorce right now.

If she divorced now, it would be playing right into the hands of those two scum.

She needed to find the right opportunity to strike back.

Since Shen Lan was so bent on climbing higher, she would let him fall completely to the bottom of the abyss.

Since Li Xuan was desperate to become the center of attention and exist on a high pedestal, she would plunge her deep into the mire.

Without her, these two should have ended up that way anyway.

Even when Shen Lan was drunk, he had once complained with regret that he had only ever been a minor section chief.

Yet without the Si family, how could the position of section chief have ever fallen to a wet-behind-the-ears novice fresh out of university?

As for Li Xuan, if not for her back then, how could she have shaken off the entanglement of her original family, and how could she have become a prominent university lecturer today?

After composing her emotions, Si Rong went home.

Mother Shen was already over sixty years old, with a thoroughly mean-spirited expression on her face.

The moment she opened her mouth, her deep dissatisfaction at Si Rong not coming home for the past two days was obvious.

"Look who it is! Why are you only coming back now? What kind of wife stays away from home day after day?"

Beside her, Shen Yun's attitude was cut from the exact same cloth as her mother's. "My sister-in-law isn't your average wife; she's a capitalist's daughter, used to doing whatever she pleases. When would she ever take us seriously?"

Si Rong lowered her gaze as she changed into her slippers, masking the contempt in her eyes before looking up with a smile. "Mom, Xiao Ming, it was my poor hospitality this time. Let me tell you some good news to make up for my faults!"

Naturally, Mother Shen was curious about this good news.

Although this daughter-in-law of hers couldn't bear children and was high-maintained, whenever she had anything good, she was always willing to give it to the two of them.

"What good news?" Shen Yun asked impatiently.

"I've found a wonderful blind date for Xiao Ming."

Si Rong truly hadn't spared any effort in this area in the past, and the men she picked were always outstanding in every way.

It was just that none of them had striking looks.

Which made them a perfect match for Shen Yun.

With Shen Lan as a county magistrate in the future, she would naturally live a comfortable, stable life of wealth.

Unfortunately, Shen Yun had never appreciated the carefully matched men she selected.

Finding them bloated and fat-faced.

Since she lacked self-awareness to that degree, she would find her a handsome one and see if she could live a good life then.

"He won't be as ugly as the last one, will he?"

Shen Yun immediately wore a look of disgust.

"Exactly, you're the sister-in-law, put some effort into it. Don't keep introducing those freaks and losers to our Xiao Yun!" Now that her son was living well, this younger daughter was her final major source of anxiety.

"Don't worry, Xiao Ming will definitely like this man. It's just that he's only a minor section chief, not as well-connected as the previous suitors."

Shen Yun didn't take that to heart. "A minor section chief, so what? Sister-in-law, don't be so snobbish. Wasn't my brother just a minor section chief back then? Now he's about to become county magistrate!"

When the time came, if she really liked the man, couldn't she just have her brother promote him?

"Then I'll arrange for you two to meet tomorrow."

Si Rong took out her phone book and made a call.

A little later, Shen Yuan came home.

Her very first words upon seeing Si Rong were about the concert tickets.

Upon learning that Si Rong hadn't bought the tickets for her yet, she was furious. "Mom! How can you go back on your word? I've already told my classmates!"

She had bragged that she would treat them to Aaron Kwok concert tickets; who in the class didn't look up to her now?

And yet her mother pulled a stunt like this?

If she couldn't treat her friends to the concert when the time came, how embarrassing would that be!

"Mom went back and asked, but your Second Uncle is away on a business trip out of town and doesn't have time. Let's wait for next time!"

Si Rong wasn't lying; her second brother was indeed away on business during this period.

But she hadn't genuinely planned to buy Shen Yuan those concert tickets in the first place.

Otherwise, if she made a call, no matter how busy her second brother was, he would have bought them for her.

It was just that she realized the two children she and Shen Lan had adopted truly matched the description from the phone call the other day; they were ungrateful wretches.

Not toward her, but toward her own family.

Upon careful thought, it was almost entirely a one-sided extraction from the Si family, yet they had never spared a single word of concern for her maternal grandparents or her two uncles.

In the past, she had simply thought they were too young, but now, judging by their attitude toward her maternal family, she could roughly guess how they would treat her in her old age.

As for breaking promises, Shen Lan's betrayal made her realize that some promises were inherently bound to be broken.
